_meta.source: FIFA. Regulations for the FIFA World Cup 26 (May 2025 edition). Article 13.
_meta.warning_to_implementer: This file overrides the tie-breaker rules described in World_Cup_2026_Build_Plan_5_Phases_v1_2.md (sections 2.6 / 3.3 / Final Core Rule Set). The build plan v1.2 has the tie-breaker ORDER wrong (it put head-to-head AFTER overall stats), names the terminal tie-breaker incorrectly (uses 'seeded random draw'; FIFA uses FIFA Ranking, no drawing of lots in 2026), and is wrong that 'fair-play data is not required' (team conduct IS in the chain). See phase_1_corrections.md.

step_1_head_to_head.name: head_to_head_points
step_1_head_to_head.description: Greatest number of points obtained in the group matches between the teams concerned.

step_1_head_to_head.name: head_to_head_goal_difference
step_1_head_to_head.description: Superior goal difference resulting from the group matches between the teams concerned.

step_1_head_to_head.name: head_to_head_goals_scored
step_1_head_to_head.description: Greatest number of goals scored in all group matches between the teams concerned.

step_2_reapply_then_overall.reapply_rule: If, after applying 1a-1c, teams still have an equal ranking, criteria 1a-1c are applied to the matches between the REMAINING tied teams only (e.g. three teams tied, one separated by head-to-head, the other two reranked using only their head-to-head match). If still no decision, proceed to 2d-2f.

criteria.name: overall_goal_difference
criteria.description: Superior goal difference in all group matches.

criteria.name: overall_goals_scored
criteria.description: Greatest number of goals scored in all group matches.

criteria.name: team_conduct_score
criteria.description: Highest team conduct score (players and team officials) relating to yellow and red cards. Higher (less negative) score ranks higher.

deductions.note: Only ONE deduction applies to a player or team official in a single match (the most severe one).

criteria.ranking_subtlety: If after a criterion (d/e/f) one team is separated but the rest remain tied, the remaining teams continue to the NEXT criterion. The second step does not restart after a partial separation.

step_3_fifa_ranking.name: fifa_ranking_latest
step_3_fifa_ranking.description: Ranked by the most recent published edition of the FIFA/Coca-Cola Men's World Ranking.

step_3_fifa_ranking.name: fifa_ranking_previous
step_3_fifa_ranking.description: Ranked by the edition immediately preceding the most recent, continuing back until a decision can be made.

within_group_ranking.drawing_of_lots_note: Unlike previous tournaments, the 2026 World Cup does NOT use drawing of lots. The FIFA Ranking chain is deterministic and guaranteed to terminate.

best_third_placed_teams_ranking.scope: Used to rank the 12 third-placed teams across all groups and select the best 8 for the Round of 32. Head-to-head criteria do NOT apply here because third-placed teams in different groups have not played each other.

criteria.name: points
criteria.description: Greatest number of points obtained in all group matches.

criteria.name: goal_difference
criteria.description: Goal difference resulting from all group matches.

criteria.name: goals_scored
criteria.description: Greatest number of goals scored in all group matches.

criteria.name: team_conduct_score
criteria.description: Highest team conduct score (calculated as in within_group_ranking step 2f).

criteria.name: fifa_ranking_latest
criteria.description: Most recent FIFA/Coca-Cola Men's World Ranking.

criteria.name: fifa_ranking_previous
criteria.description: Earlier FIFA Ranking editions, continually until a decision can be made.

simulator_implementation_notes.simulation_scope: The Monte Carlo simulator does NOT simulate cards/disciplinary events per match, so team_conduct_score cannot be computed inside a simulation.
simulator_implementation_notes.tie_break_collapse_policy: When a tie reaches the team_conduct_score step inside a simulation, collapse the remaining criteria into a deterministic, seeded tiebreaker derived from a pre-tournament prior (e.g., the team's pre-tournament Elo). This is reproducible, defensible, and avoids fake-data fabrication.
simulator_implementation_notes.alternative_collapse_policy: Acceptable: use the team's pre-tournament FIFA Ranking directly, since that is the official chain (3g) and is data we already have. This is preferred over Elo for fidelity to FIFA's chain.
simulator_implementation_notes.frequency_of_deep_ties: Ties that survive points + head-to-head + overall GD + overall GS are vanishingly rare in simulation (<1% of group instances). The choice of collapse policy has negligible effect on aggregate champion probabilities.
simulator_implementation_notes.what_to_disclose_on_methodology_page: The simulator implements the full Article 13 chain through overall goals scored, then collapses subsequent tie-breakers (team conduct + FIFA ranking chain) by ranking still-tied teams by their pre-tournament FIFA Ranking. Drawing of lots is NOT used (FIFA does not use it for 2026). Document the collapse policy honestly.
